correctness.rationale: Dyadic comparability identifies the same reciprocal series in both halves. Convergence uniformly controls reciprocal fiber weights, giving L1 Fourier integrability and the L2 periodization estimate used in the periodic-gap uniqueness construction. Under divergence, the endpoint dyadic blocks have squared weighted energy O(a_j); inverse-energy convex averaging reduces the squared norm to O(1/sum a_j^{-1}) while preserving interpolation and local uniform smallness, so the standard successive-correction construction yields nonuniqueness.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2017 result states the positive theorem for Sobolev alpha>1/2, and the recent arXiv:2609.20805 proves the pure-power threshold is sharp for S=A+Z. No matching reciprocal-weight dichotomy or beta=1 logarithmic refinement was located in the inspected sources or searches. The residual risk is an unindexed parallel observation because the source preprint is extremely recent.

value.rationale: The result resolves the second-order boundary at the newly established critical Sobolev exponent: |t| log^beta(e+|t|) supports uniformly discrete uniqueness exactly for beta>1. The broader reciprocal-series formulation explains both the positive periodization threshold and the optimal inverse-energy averaging in the counterexample construction.
